summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sewage Treatment Plants process wastewater across two core phases: (1) Primary Physical treatment removing floating debris and grit; (2) Secondary Biological treatment using aerobic microbial flocs in aeration tanks to consume organic waste and slash BOD (>90%). Activated sludge settles and feeds anaerobic digesters.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Stepwise STP Mechanics
1. **Primary Treatment (Physical Separation)**:
   - **Sequential Filtration**: Sewage is passed through wire mesh screens of progressively finer pore sizes to remove large floating plastic, cloth, and paper debris.
   - **Sedimentation**: Sewage enters grit chambers and primary settling tanks where heavy inorganic grit (sand, soil, pebbles) and settleable organic solids settle under gravity.
   - **Products**: Settled solid mass forms **Primary Sludge**; the overlying supernatant liquid forms **Primary Effluent**.
2. **Secondary / Biological Treatment**:
   - Primary effluent is channeled into massive, open **Aeration Tanks** that are continuously agitated mechanically with air pumped in under pressure.
   - **Flocs Formation**: Aerobic conditions stimulate the rapid proliferation of **Flocs** (mesh-like aggregates of aerobic bacterial cells intertwined with network-forming fungal filaments).
   - **Organic Matter Oxidation**: Aerobic heterotrophic microbes consume dissolved organic pollutants as respiratory substrates, slashing the **Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)** by $>90\%$.
   - **Settling Tank & Activated Sludge**: When BOD is sufficiently low, the effluent is passed into a settling tank where flocs sediment under quiescent conditions to form **Activated Sludge**.
   - **Sludge Partitioning**: A small fraction ($<5\%$) of activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as an **inoculum**; the remaining bulk is pumped into **Anaerobic Sludge Digesters**.

### 6.2 Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) Invariants
- **Definition**: BOD is the amount of dissolved oxygen (in $\text{mg } \text{O}_2/\text{L}$) consumed by aerobic microorganisms to completely oxidize the biodegradable organic matter present in a one-liter water sample.
- **Direct Correlation**: $\text{Higher BOD} \iff \text{Greater Organic Pollution Load} \iff \text{Lower Dissolved Oxygen (DO)}$.
- Unpolluted river water: $\text{BOD} < 1\text{--}2\text{ mg/L}$; Untreated domestic sewage: $\text{BOD} > 400\text{ mg/L}$.

### 6.3 National River Cleaning Programs
- To combat catastrophic pollution of Indian rivers due to untreated sewage influx, the Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the **Ganga Action Plan (GAP, 1985)** and the **Yamuna Action Plan (YAP)** to construct hundreds of municipal STPs.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD)
conceptBreakdown.title: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD)
conceptBreakdown.content: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) measures the total quantity of oxygen required to chemically oxidize all organic compounds (both biodegradable and non-biodegradable) using a strong chemical oxidant like potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7 in acidic medium); COD is always greater than or equal to BOD.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Tertiary Sewage Treatment
conceptBreakdown.title: Tertiary Sewage Treatment
conceptBreakdown.content: Tertiary treatment is an advanced physicochemical process that removes dissolved inorganic nutrients (phosphates and nitrates) using chemical precipitation, sand/carbon filtration, and disinfects final effluent using Chlorination or UV radiation before discharge.
